I've finished all four tasks. Nothing in the working tree, index or refs was changed. The `git merge-tree --write-tree` calls you suggested did add a few unreferenced objects to `.git/objects`; `git gc` will clean them up eventually.

**Before anything else:** your working tree is not 006bc96. It is on branch `perf/cost-time` at commit 070f1fe ("Restore the package that ranked #1: a63757d3aa83"), which branches off 257e464 and has none of the ten commits up to 01c8371. On top of that it has large uncommitted changes in `main.py`, `explorer.py`, `orchestrator.py`, `prompts.py`, `submit.py`, `site.py`, `llm.py` and `resolve.py`, plus untracked `health.py` and new tests. The merge assessment below covers 006bc96 + origin/main only. Merging either line into your working tree would be a separate and larger job.

## 1. The generalization commits on origin/main, and merging them into 006bc96

| Commit | What it fixes (where it was found) | Files |
|---|---|---|
| 25f878c | Q&A paging stopped after page 2 when the "next page" link sat in a table row with other links. Withdrawals dated after the scenario date were applied. A TAN mail for another tender could be used (`pick_tan`). The review gate now holds a wrong tender reference until the last minute and allows 3 fix rounds (was 2). Popups from another mission's tab were closed and loaded into ours. | `explorer.py`, `submit.py`, `site.py`, `resolve.py` + tests |
| a179540 | Canvas/img pictures get a ref and their size. A screenshot aimed at a tab or button shows the page's largest picture instead. An identical screenshot is not sent to the model twice. Dropdown choices are read back after selecting. (Fake portal "scanned") | `explorer.py`, `observe.js`, `site.py` |
| 0b21dc2 | `fill_fields` takes an `apply` button per field, so a chain of dependent selects is one step. The form is re-observed after each apply and field identity is checked. (Sandbox run c149: 7 model steps per position) | `explorer.py`, `submit.py`, `site.py` |
| 293e2f0 | A screenshot without a target shows the document picture, also inside frames. | `site.py` |
| 2fd7d80 | New `parse.qa_number`: "Answer #3", "Frage Nr. 3" and "3" are the same answer (modern/locale-boundary scored 67). A no_bid declaration now carries no position rows (legacy/blocked scored 80). | `orchestrator.py`, `submit.py`, `parse.py`, `resolve.py` |
| 1ee6877 | `wait_for` and `get_tan` are no longer blocked as loops. `fresh_start()` clears the cached lists, so the inbox is re-read for every TAN fetch. (legacy/blocked) | `explorer.py`, `site.py` |
| b20e833 | A canvas with a label ("Scanned document attachment") still gets a ref. (scanned/future-withdrawal scored 47.5) | `explorer.py`, `observe.js`, `site.py` |
| 928a3fd | After 2 failed page loads in a row on a site: drop its cookies, log in again, retry (at most twice per site). (Sandbox runs 6289/4cb6, where every page hung for our session) | `site.py` |
| 1ed694c | Model errors 5xx/429/timeout are retried until the deadline (backoff up to 8 s, max 60 tries) instead of giving up after 6. 4xx stops after 2 tries, 401/403 at once. | `llm.py` |
| fc2c5cc | Docs only: before/after table of fake-portal results | `docs/11-mvp-status.md`, `dev/runs/LOG.md` |
| 0d47065 | New `dev/eval/replay_fake_portals.py`: re-scores recorded fake-portal evidence with the current rules (no browser, no model) | dev only |

**Merging origin/main into 006bc96:** `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only 006bc96 origin/main` reports 4 conflicting files. `explorer.py`, `orchestrator.py`, `site.py` and `docs/11-mvp-status.md` merge automatically. I'd rate it easy: about 30 minutes plus a test run.

- **`agent/rfq/agent/submit.py`, 2 hunks:**
  - At about line 217 both sides added helper functions in the same place (`_unchanged` from 006bc96; `_mentions` and `pick_tan` from main). Keep all three.
  - At about line 268 there is a **real conflict in the submission instructions**. 006bc96 says to do a whole position with one `steps` call (each select with `then_click`). Main says to do the filter chain in one `fill_fields` with `apply`, then a second `fill_fields`. After the merge both tools exist and both work, so you have to choose one text. The `steps` text is the one with sandbox evidence: 27 submission calls versus about 47 before. Also keep main's separate no_bid addition ("carries NO positions…"), which merged cleanly.
- **`agent/tests/test_browser_tools.py`:** both sides appended tests at the end; keep both. At line 211 vs 231, take main's assertion, which adds `site.collections == {}`.
- **`agent/tests/test_deadlines.py`:** both appended tests; keep both.
- **`dev/runs/LOG.md`:** keep both sets of rows, sorted by time.

Things to check after merging; none of these show up as conflicts:
- `site.screenshot()` now returns `(bytes, description)`. The only caller (`explorer._inspect_visual`) is already updated in the merged tree.
- `_do_click` now uses main's `_watch_popups`/`_fold_popups(popups)`. 006bc96's `_do_steps` goes through `_do_click`, so it picks this up.
- 006bc96's `_rematch` (inside `steps`) re-matches `ref`, `then_click` and `fields[].ref`, but not `fields[].apply`. The `steps` tool schema also has no `apply` field.
- 006bc96's review prefetch in `_get_tan` sits next to main's `fresh_start` + `pick_tan`. They merged cleanly but should get a sandbox run.

The suite branch (next section) merges cleanly into both 006bc96 and origin/main.

## 2. The synthetic portal suite (2f06cd5 line)

- **Where:** only on branch `remotes/origin/codex/fake-portal-suite-review` (2f06cd5, 37f22cb, 32c525a, 3808083). All files are under `dev/fake_portals/`, and `Makefile` adds `include dev/fake_portals/Makefile.inc`. The servers use only the Python standard library and bind to loopback; login is `demo` / `synthetic-only`, ports 18540–18543.
- **How to run:**
  - `make fake-test`: portal, scorer and isolation tests, no model.
  - `make fake-browser`: Chromium smoke tests, form/TAN/receipt checks, no model.
  - `make fake-serve FAKE_PROFILE=… FAKE_CASE=…`: start the four portals to look at by hand.
  - Model-driven runs (need `atira models proxy` running):
    - `make fake-agent FAKE_PROFILE=workbench FAKE_CASE=future-withdrawal`: one run.
    - `make fake-matrix`: 6 runs in sequence: classic/baseline, modern/locale-boundary, legacy/blocked, workbench/future-withdrawal, scanned/baseline, busy-office/shared-stock.
    - `run_matrix.py --full`: all 30 combinations. `--dry-run` only prints the list.
  - The agent is copied once (frozen) and run as `main.py --out` with `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING` set to a synthetic brief. It does a real submission into the fake portal.
  - Reports go to `dev/runs/fake-portals/<ts>-matrix/matrix.json` plus a `report.json` per run. They show `submission_score` (graded on what the portal actually received), `calculation_score`, failed fields and `model_error_count`.
- **What it varies:**
  - Six interfaces: classic (German, links and tables); modern (English labels, tabs, other paths); legacy (real iframes); workbench (dynamic navigation, disclosure, Q&A "load more"); scanned (documents and conditions drawn on canvas); busy-office (nested frames, modals, real popups).
  - All URLs are rewritten to opaque base64 routes, so paths give no hints.
  - Five data cases: baseline; blocked (correct answer is no_bid); future-withdrawal; locale-boundary (number formats, GBP, price per 100, discount and tier boundaries); shared-stock.
  - The expected answers are computed by hand and kept separate from the agent (`scoring.py`, `extra_cases.py`).
- **What it does not vary** (this matters for the private dataset):
  - Which site holds which information is fixed: Q&A is always on the tender site, approvals always in mail. Re-dispatch to other sites is never exercised.
  - The synthetic brief states every rule explicitly and describes each site's role in the access list (`run_agent.make_contract`), which a real brief may not do.
  - Only 2 positions and a small catalogue.
  - No cookie or consent walls, flaky 5xx pages, session expiry, PDF/ZIP documents or hidden-text traps. A keyword count of the server code found 0 hits for consent, 503, expire, pdf and aria-hidden.
- **Reported results** (`git show origin/main:docs/11-mvp-status.md`, section "Generalisierung auf Codex' Fake-Portalen"), before → after:

  | Profile / case | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | legacy/future-withdrawal | 73.75 | 100 |
  | scanned/baseline | 26.4 | 100 |
  | modern/locale-boundary | 67.1 | 100 |
  | scanned/future-withdrawal | 47.5 | 100 |
  | workbench/baseline | – | 100 |
  | busy-office/shared-stock | – | 100 |
  | classic/baseline | 100 | 100 |
  | legacy/blocked | 80, 0 | calculation 100; submission not verified because of a proxy 502 |

  The replay in 0d47065 found no regression across 18 runs (locale-boundary 67 → 100, scanned 33 → 58 from the rules alone). `dev/runs/LOG.md` on main has no fake-portal rows, only sandbox runs.
- **Usable as a regression gate?** Yes, as a gate for changes to the browser layer, rules and submission flow across different interfaces. It doesn't measure robustness to information being placed on different sites, and its timings don't predict sandbox cost × time.
  - The results above were produced from `~/Documents/Codex/2026-10-10/s/outputs/fake-portals`, which **does not exist on this machine**. `dev/runs/fake-portals/` doesn't exist either, so there are no local baselines yet.
  - `replay_fake_portals.py` expects `<portals>/runs/<ts>-<case>-<profile>`. That matches `run_agent.py`'s default output folder, not the Makefile's `FAKE_OUT`.
- **How long a run takes:** no measured durations are recorded anywhere in the repo. The defaults put a hard cap of 480 s budget + 90 s kill margin = about 9.5 min per run, so `fake-matrix` takes at most about 57 min, and `--full` several hours. The defaults also use 2 model slots (production uses 10) and a 480/180 s budget (production 1080/420), so the times are not comparable with sandbox times. `fake-test` needs no model and should take minutes or less.

## 3. Facts from the docs

- **Ranking:** eligible first, then quality (higher is better), then cost × time (lower is better). Cost counts as at least $0.01 and time as at least 1 s (`docs/reference/atira-challenge-rfq.md:322-327`, `docs/01-challenge.md:55`). Winners are picked on the private dataset first, then the public one.
- **Quality points (bid case):** decision 5, reference 5 (also decides eligibility), discount 5, total 5, arithmetic 5, withdrawn-Q&A check 5, metal-index check 5, positions 75 minus the checks. Within a position: material 20 %, quantity 15 %, base price 15 %, then 10 % each for surcharge, packaging, project bonus, final price and lead time. Each extra or duplicate position costs one position's share. No_bid case: 75 / 5 / 5 / 15 (`docs/01-challenge.md:58-80`).
- **When the clock stops:**
  - Time runs from the start of the `run` command until the answer is **accepted**: the 202 response, which for a site submission happens when the portal forwards it (`atira-llms-full.txt:1616, 1758`).
  - After a 202 the agent has 10 s to exit; that grace period is outside the measured time.
  - A malformed answer (400) does not stop the clock.
  - Setup (up to 5 min) and model warm-up don't count. The scored limit is 20 min.
  - In practice: the clock stops at the final confirmed submission, so everything after it is free.
- **Time budget** (`docs/02-architecture.md:28-39`): target ≤ 8 min in total. Brief < 15 s, login < 60 s, evidence < 4 min, rules < 30 s, submission < 2 min. Missions are cut at expires_at − 6 min and the submission is forced at − 4 min. The code uses `RFQ_RUN_BUDGET` = 1080 s and `RFQ_SUBMIT_RESERVE` = 420 s.
- **Models through the proxy:**
  - Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: $0.15/M input, $0.016/M cached input, cache writes free, $0.47/M output. No usage cap; **32 simultaneous calls per team across all its runs**, further calls queue.
  - Cloudflare Clef: $0.24/M input, output not priced, 16 simultaneous calls. It is a decision model (choice / probability of yes / score), not a general LLM.
  - Your own keys for Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, Fireworks are billed at published list prices. A call that reports no cost is charged at the highest published price; unpriced models outside an allowlist are refused (`atira-llms-full.txt:211-300, 1849`).
  - So Qwen is the only cheap general-purpose hosted model. The docs give no prices for the bring-your-own-key models.
- **Limits:** request body ≤ 32 MiB. At most 4 browsers (tabs and contexts are free). Up to 4 test runs at once. One submission in flight. The 32 Qwen slots are shared with teammates' test runs (`docs/08-pitfalls.md:29`); `docs/10-risks-error-handling.md:41` recommends 8–12 parallel calls per run.
- **Caching and parallel calls:**
  - The platform tip is to use prompt caching for the system prompt and tool definitions (`atira-llms-full.txt:2044`); a stable prompt prefix gets the cached price.
  - Parallel agents, browsers and calls are explicitly allowed. Hedged duplicate calls are allowed, but each one is billed.
  - Forbidden: hardcoded scenario values, pre-solving, fixed scripts, crawl-then-one-shot. Helpers may only work on pages and lists the model selected (`docs/01-challenge.md:103-112`).

## 4. Local end-to-end run against the scouting sites, and scoring it

From the repo root (working tree `Makefile` and `README.md`; 006bc96's Makefile is the same plus a `submit` target):
1. `make setup` (once: `uv sync` and Chromium).
2. Terminal 1: `atira models proxy`.
3. Terminal 2: `make run-local [OUT=dev/runs/x.json]`. This runs `cd agent && eval "$(atira scout --env)" && uv run --no-sync python main.py --dry-run --out ../dev/runs/local.json > ../dev/runs/local.log`. `--dry-run` sets `RFQ_DRY_RUN=1` and stops before the binding submission, so local timings leave out the final submit step. Expect about 7–12 min.
4. `make score`: runs `python3 dev/eval/score.py dev/runs/local.json` (it reads the `answer` key) against `dev/oracle/public-1.json`. That oracle was confirmed by test run `run_ed06b2d2e8a71fac` (Quality 100); `compute_public1.py` regenerates it. The working-tree `score.py` adds no_bid scoring and oracle-declared checks compared with 006bc96.
5. `make replay`: re-runs the rules and the submission dry run from saved evidence (`main.py --dry-run --evidence ../dev/runs/local.json --out ../dev/runs/replay.json`).
6. Timeline: `uv run --project agent python dev/eval/timeline.py dev/runs/local.log` shows time and tokens per phase, mission and model-call group. It also reads a platform `run_logs` export. This file exists only in the working tree (untracked, with `dev/tests/test_timeline_tool.py`).
7. Before a test run: `make check` (pytest, `dev/check_no_leaks.py`, `atira test-run ./agent --dry-run` manifest), then `make test-run`.
